subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin/API config-write veto hook, and what ordering, redaction, trust, timeout, recursion, and failure semantics should it have across RPC and shared config mutation paths?
rationale: Source inspection proves the seam is missing, but this would create a new plugin-facing security boundary over persisted configuration writes, so automation cannot safely choose the policy.

options.title: Design guarded config-write hook
options.body: Add a narrow pre-persistence hook covering `config.set`, `config.patch`, `config.apply`, and shared mutation helpers with explicit redaction, timeout, recursion, and rejection semantics.

options.title: Limit to built-in validation
options.body: Keep mandatory config protection in core validation, SecretRef preflight, agent allowlists, and doctor checks, while documenting external validators as optional helpers only.

options.title: Fold into broader preflight RFC
options.body: Defer this hook until the broader config validation/preflight direction chooses one shared validation and failure contract.

recommendation.title: Design guarded config-write hook
recommendation.body: Add a narrow pre-persistence hook covering `config.set`, `config.patch`, `config.apply`, and shared mutation helpers with explicit redaction, timeout, recursion, and rejection semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They already framed this issue as an unresolved config validation/mutation boundary and have recent adjacent config/security history.
